source_text: This module covers market conduct: insider trading and conflicts of interest.
It applies to every employee, not only to those on an investment desk.
Material non-public information is information a reasonable investor would want before trading.
It becomes material long before it becomes a press release.
Never trade on material non-public information, and never pass it to anyone outside your need-to-know group.
Passing it on is called tipping, and it is an offence even if you never trade yourself.
A conversation overheard in a lift is still information you now hold.
If you receive it by accident, tell Compliance the same day.
Personal account dealing must be pre-cleared through the approved workflow.
Pre-clearance expires; an approval from last week does not cover a trade today.
A conflict of interest is any situation where your interest could influence your judgement.
It does not have to be financial, and it does not have to be deliberate.
A family member working at a counterparty is a conflict to declare, not to hide.
Gifts and hospitality above the threshold must be declared before you accept them.
Declaring is routine; failing to declare is the misconduct.
Do not discuss client holdings in public places, including office lifts and cabs.
Confidential means the information stays inside the group that needs it to do its work.
Our record retention rules also cover messages on approved channels.
Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.
When a situation is unclear, Compliance would rather answer a question than open an investigation.
